methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $47M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Pivotal, a Growth-stage transportation company founded by Marcus Leng and backed by Page, is the subject of this valuation analysis. The sector includes three identified private peers—Rivian, The Boring Company, and Einride—though no public comparables exist in the narrow peer set. The scarcity of same-stage and similarly-tiered private transportation companies limits traditional peer median benchmarking.

A single applicable method was employed: Stage-Progression analysis. Using Pivotal's $47M total capital raised as a base proxy, a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of the Growth stage transition yields an implied valuation of $56M. This methodology directly reflects observed fundraising history and stage-appropriate return expectations rather than relying on sparse peer data.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $48M to $64M, with a median estimate of $56M. The $16M spread reflects methodological constraints: the insufficiency of same-stage and adjacent-stage peers in Transportation prevents peer-median calibration, leaving stage progression as the sole quantitative anchor. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 1.2x multiplier for Pivotal's specific risk profile and the absence of public market reference points. A fuller analysis would benefit from adjacent-sector peer multiples or forward revenue projections, neither of which is available in the current dataset.
